To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PI3Kα/β are expressed in cardiac cells and that PI3Kβ is activated by ATP in these cells.
PI3Ks are crucial regulators of cell Ca2+ homeoostasis in cardiomyocytes, and that the specific PI3Kγ isoform mediates this effect in the cardiac cell.

PI3Kα/PI3Kγ are crucial regulators of the spontaneous Ca2+ activity of the cardiomyocyte, and PI3Kα is involved in the regulation of the cardiomyocytes' contractility, whereas PI3Kγ is involved in the cardiomyocytes spontaneous Ca2+ oscillations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel role for PI3K in the regulation of cardiac cell Ca2+ homeo-stasis.
the identification of PI3K isoforms in cardiac cells and their role in the regulation of the cardiac autonomic activity, and the elucidation of the signaling pathway that mediates this effect.
the identification of a specific role for PI3Ks and of a specific PI3Kγ isoform in the regulation of cell Ca2+ homeo-stasis in cardiomyocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PI3Kγ-Tec pathway is a specific and crucial pathway in the purineregulated Ca2+ splicing of the cardiomyocyte.

PI3Kα is the most important isoform in the heart, and PI3Kβ is the most important in the vascular smooth muscle cells.

the activation of the Tec kinase by the PI3Kγ is a crucial event in the purinergically induced Ca2+ splicing.
PI3Kα/β are important for cell growth, survival, and migration; PI3Kγ for cell secretion, cell Ca2+ regulation, and cell migration.

The main takeaway from our work is that
PI3K isoforms have distinct roles and that PI3Kα/β/γ is a specific regulator of cardiac Ca2+ signaling.
PI3Ks are not all equal and that the PI3Kγ isoform has a specific role in purinergic regulation and in the control of Ca2+ homeo-stasis in cardiac cells.
